rv.q: "Primary Trust" is a tonic for ailing spirits.
Booth's deeply sympathetic rendering of a good man navigating a life of crises is 95 minutes of sublimity.
Primary Trust is the sort of play that reminds us why theater matters.
In its unassuming way, 'Primary Trust' is one of the most moving things on an L.A. stage this season.
I advise you to run, not walk to the Mark Taper Forum to catch this most extraordinary of Pulitzer Prize honorees.
Primary Trust is moving and fulfilling, filled with well-painted characters, including one with mental illness.

If this sounds a bit too low-key to be involving, it isn’t. Booth’s writing is filled with wry tender humor, the kind that comes from understanding the lonely human heart and the behaviors of ordinary folk who deal each day with the aches and pains of getting by.
